unit: The Water Cycle and Earth’s Resources
length: Term 1 Weeks 7–9 · 6 lessons and the topic test
description: Students model the water cycle as the way Earth renews its fresh water, then classify Earth’s resources as renewable or non-renewable and weigh up how sustainably we use them. They compare the benefits and risks of extracting resources and of producing energy from fossil fuels and renewables, and finish by auditing energy use in a household, linking it to appliances, building design, season and climate.
notes: **Audit changes:** a learning intention for the benefits and risks of resource extraction and energy production (VC2S8U09) is in Lessons 3 and 5; the household energy audit (VC2S8U16), now a Year 7 descriptor, is a new Lesson 6 in the empty T1 W9 Lesson 1 slot.
Week 9 is short (PTSC Thursday, Good Friday), so the topic test sits in Lesson 2 of that week as the scope and sequence has it.
**No site unit or slide decks exist for this unit yet**, so explicit instruction and worksheet links are placeholders.

achievement.text: Distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources, including water renewed by the water cycle; evaluate how sustainably resources are used; compare the benefits and risks of resource extraction and energy production; explain how household energy use depends on appliances, building design, season and climate, using an energy audit.
Make and record observations of a model; collect and organise data in tables and graphs; analyse patterns; communicate findings and recommendations for an audience.

Discuss the ethical, environmental, social and economic considerations of a socio-scientific issue (mining and energy choices); analyse how science communication shapes viewpoints and policies (energy ratings and advice).

descriptors.text: Earth’s resources, including water, are renewable or non-renewable; their sustainable use, and the benefits and risks of resource extraction and energy production
Household energy use, assessed by an energy audit; depends on appliances, building design, season and climate
Energy exists in different forms; energy transfers and transformations, and their efficiency (energy sources and appliances)
Proposed scientific responses to socio-scientific issues impact society and involve ethical, environmental, social and economic considerations
Science communication shapes individual viewpoints, community policies and regulations
Science inquiry — recording data (I03); representing and analysing it (I04–I05); communicating findings (I08)

prepare: Opening question: where does the water from your tap come from, and where does it go?
Recall changes of state from the Particle Model unit (evaporation, condensation).
review: Exit questions each lesson; Resources glossary flashcards.
diff: Labelled water-cycle diagram to complete; resource sort cards; a renewable / non-renewable table with a worked first row in red.
Energy audit with a pre-filled appliance list and a calculation frame (power × hours).
extension: Compare the full life-cycle impacts of two energy sources.
Recommend changes to a household from the audit data and estimate the saving.

lessons.title: What is the water cycle?
li: Describe the processes of the water cycle — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection and transpiration.
Explain why water is a renewable resource, and why fresh water is still limited.
sc: I can draw and label the water cycle and explain each process using changes of state.
explicit: {{PH:PPT link — What is the Water Cycle}}
review: Exit question: why is fresh water limited if water is renewable?

lessons.title: Lab: water cycle in a bag
li: Model the water cycle and observe evaporation and condensation.
sc: I can match each part of my model to a stage of the water cycle and say one limitation of the model.

prac.name: Water cycle in a bag — sealed bag of water taped to a sunny window, observed over several days
prac.si: Make and record observations of a model over time, and evaluate the model (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Identify evaporation, condensation and precipitation in the model (VC2S8U09).

prac.risk: {{PH:RiskAssess link — water cycle in a bag}}

review: Observations checked over the following lessons

lessons.title: Resources
li: Classify Earth’s resources as renewable or non-renewable.
Describe how resources such as metals, coal and gas are extracted.
Evaluate the benefits and risks of resource extraction (VC2S8U09).
sc: I can sort resources as renewable or non-renewable and give one benefit and one risk of mining.
guided: {{PH:worksheet — resource sort and extraction case study}}

lessons.title: Renewability and sustainability
li: Explain what makes the use of a resource sustainable.
Describe ways to conserve resources: reduce, reuse, recycle and substitute.
sc: I can judge whether a use of a resource is sustainable and suggest an improvement.
review: Exit question: how could the school use water more sustainably?

lessons.title: Energy and renewable energy
li: Describe how electricity is produced from fossil fuels and from renewable sources.
Compare the benefits and risks of different ways of producing energy (VC2S8U09).
sc: I can compare two energy sources by cost, reliability and environmental impact.

lessons.title: Household energy audit
li: Assess household energy use with an energy audit.
Explain how energy use depends on appliances, building design, season and climate (VC2S8U16).
Explain how energy-rating labels and public advice shape people’s choices (VC2S8H04).
Communicate a recommendation to a household using the audit data (VC2S8I08).
sc: I can calculate the energy an appliance uses and recommend two changes that would reduce a household’s energy use.
explicit: Worked example: energy = power × time, from an appliance label

prac.name: Energy audit — appliances, ratings and hours of use for a home (or the classroom), with seasonal changes
prac.si: Collect and organise data in a table; analyse which uses the most energy; communicate recommendations (VC2S8I04, VC2S8I05, VC2S8I08).
prac.su: Explain how appliances, building design, season and climate affect household energy use (VC2S8U16).

guided: Homework: complete the audit at home

lessons.title: Topic test
li: Show what I know about the water cycle, resources, sustainability and energy use.
sc: I can answer questions on the unit under test conditions.
